title: Alethia: a Foundational Encoder for Voice Deepfakes
claim: A masked student encoder feeds one shared embedding into two parallel objectives, continuous teacher-embedding prediction and generative spectrogram reconstruction.
layout: Single panel, bottom-to-top flow, branching into two parallel branches with a top waveform input
description: A single vertical pipeline that reads from bottom to top. At the bottom, a black waveform is interrupted by gray [Mask] blocks, labeled 'CNN Mask'. An arrow leads up to the 'Student Layer Mask' stack, which shows rows of blue circles. Some circles are pale with dashed outlines to mark masked positions. Above it is a green rounded bar labeled 'Bottleneck embeddings', and the flow splits into two branches. The left branch points to a row of six yellow-to-brown vertical pills labeled Layer 1 through Layer N-1. These are the 'Continuous teacher embeddings (50Hz)'. A gray arrow from a snowflake-marked, frozen 'Teacher Model' feeds them. The right branch goes through a 'Decoder' trapezoid and a dashed 'Flow-matching' arrow to a viridis-colored spectrogram (100Hz). A clean waveform at the top sends gray arrows to both the teacher and the spectrogram target.
caption: Pretraining framework of Alethia. Alethia encoder receives masked waveform and projects it into layer-averaged bottleneck embeddings. These embeddings are then fed in parallel to (1) a bottleneck masked embedding prediction branch which predicts different teacher layer embeddings, and (2) a spectrogram reconstruction branch to predict the velocity field calculated between the target spectrogram and the decoded spectrogram. The ground-truth embeddings and spectrogram are both obtained from the unmasked waveform.
abstract: Existing voice deepfake detection and localization models rely heavily on representations extracted from speech foundation models (SFMs). However, downstream finetuning has now reached a state of diminishing returns. In this paper, we shift the focus to pretraining and propose a novel recipe that combines bottleneck masked embedding prediction with flow-matching based spectrogram reconstruction. The outcome, Alethia, is the first foundational audio encoder for various voice deepfake detection and localization tasks. We evaluate on $5$ different tasks with $56$ benchmark datasets, and note Alethia significantly outperforms state-of-the-art SFMs with superior robustness to real-world perturbations and zero-shot generalization to unseen domains (e.g., singing deepfakes). We also demonstrate the limitation of discrete targets in masked token prediction, and show the importance of continuous embedding prediction and generative pretraining for capturing deepfake artifacts.
